2017_103_011717org_regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education's organizational and regular meeting of January 17, 2017 at the Services Building — the first meeting of a reconstituted Board, with Gottlieb and Hammond replacing Ida Edmunds and Wendy Underwood, who had retired the previous month after 31 and 11 years. The organizational half elects officers and re-designates the treasurer, depositories and legal counsel; the regular half establishes an Employment Dispute Resolution Plan sending all nonunion employment claims to binding arbitration instead of court, awards $101,162.00 of portable testing tables and chairs, and authorizes the sale of 18.08 acres in Section 23 — on a resolution whose purchase price is still printed as "$x,xxx,xxx."

**Meeting**
Organizational and regular meeting, January 17, 2017, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**The organizational half**
Dr. Machesky's agenda memo sets out the sequence: elect an acting chairperson to conduct the meeting until a president is elected — "past practice has been that the previous year's president conducts this part of the meeting" — appoint Judy Holmes temporary secretary, then elect president, vice president and secretary in turn. Nominations need not be seconded, a motion and support close them, and **four votes are required for election**. The treasurer is appointed annually as a nonvoting officer; the assistant superintendent of business services has served in that role and the superintendent recommends continuing it.

Remaining organizational items establish fund depositories and the investment resolution, designate legal counsel — Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Lusk Albertson; LaPointe & Associates, P.C.; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; and Beier Howlett, P.C. — designate the superintendent deputy secretary, designate a person for posting notices, and adopt the 2017 meeting schedule. Twelve depository institutions are named, with Rick West as treasurer; checks carry his facsimile signature, and in emergencies his handwritten signature or Superintendent Machesky's on the General Fund and Payroll accounts at Bank of America.

The schedule document is the prior year's calendar overtyped rather than retyped: it reads "Tuesday, January 1917, 2016 2017 (Organizational & Regular Meeting)" and so on down the page, with both years and both dates visible in each line. The depositories agenda line likewise still reads 2015/16 and 2016/17.

**Recognition**
Board Recognition Month. Each Board member receives a **ONE Troy ensemble** — a basket with t-shirts, hats, water bottles, mugs, pens, pencils and baked goods, each item a symbol of one of the district's schools. The script ties the gift to the ONE TROY idea developed when Machesky was selected to lead the district: "we are not merely a district of schools, but ONE school district, with a single mission and a single focus on student achievement for ALL."

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the December 6, 2016 workshop and special meeting, the December 20, 2016 meeting, and the November 2016 Treasurer's Report.

**What the December 20 minutes record**
Miletti and Superintendent Machesky were both absent; Deputy Superintendent Mark Dziatczak sat in. The meeting honored **Ida Edmunds, retiring after more than 31 years, and Wendy Underwood, after more than 11** — their final meeting. Each received a framed letter from Senator Gary Peters' office, a gift from the district, and a proclamation signed by the Oakland County Board of Commissioners, presented in person by County Commissioner Wade Fleming.

The Board also awarded Bond Construction Bid Pack #18 — $2,992,853.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund and $369,527.00 from the Food Service Budget, **totalling $3,362,380.00** across Blue Star demolition $14,100.00, Hewett exterior doors $537,505.00, Paint Plus painting and floors $35,217.00, Stafford Smith food service equipment $100,063.00, CSM mechanical (Barnard, Bemis, Wass, IAE) $873,173.00, Contrast mechanical (Admin, Boulan, Larson) $418,000.00, MCMI temperature controls $392,150.00, Great Lakes Power electrical $686,500.00 and $305,672.00 of contingency — and a roofing bid of **$1,290,978.00** (J. D. Chandler $300,300.00, Royal West $873,316.00, 10% contingency $117,362.00). It adopted the Board of Education Bylaws and Policies. Mary Bogush of Royal Oak addressed the Board about the Section 1 property — the same speaker who would return through 2018 as that land came up for sale.

**Treasurer's Report — November 2016**
Total check disbursements are $6,814,915.65 — General Fund group $5,499,172.59, Special Revenue $512,654.63, Other Funds $803,088.43 — with the General Fund (101) itself at $4,954,666.13. Adding $1,962,408.22 of wire transfers, $169,245.62 of P-Card purchases and $20,707.64 of ACH debits, less $70.00 of prior period voids, total disbursements in period are $8,967,207.13.

**Personnel — the arbitration plan**
The Board establishes an Employment Dispute Resolution Plan covering **all applicants for employment, all substitute employees, all nonunion employees and all nonunion administrators and supervisors**. Its stated purpose is fair, efficient and timely resolution of claims arising out of application, employment or cessation of employment, providing a forum in which disputes "may be resolved **exclusively by final and binding arbitration rather than litigation**."

The authority cited is MCL 380.11a of the Revised School Code. Arbitration is administered by the American Arbitration Association under Michigan's Uniform Arbitration Act and the AAA Employment Arbitration Rules, with judgment entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. The plan includes a **collective actions waiver** requiring employees to arbitrate individually. It does not restrict anyone from filing with a state, federal or other governmental administrative agency — it applies only to local, state and federal court proceedings.

**Business**

| Item | Amount | Fund |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Section 23 property, 18.08 +/- acres | **not filled in** | — |
| Portable testing tables and chairs | Global Equipment Co., Inc. — $101,162.00 | General Fund |

The Section 23 item covers 18.08 +/- acres of vacant land adjacent to Raintree Park, Sidwell Numbers 20-23-200-007, -008 and -009. Seven proposals were received and examined with legal counsel Clark Hill and consultant Great Northern. But the resolution as printed names neither buyer nor price: it recommends sale "to the approved developer in the amount of $x,xxx,xxx," recites a proposal from "approved developer (the 'Purchaser')" at "proposed amount ($x,xxx,xxx) Dollars with an earnest money deposit of proposed amount ($xx,xxx) Dollars," and authorizes Dr. Machesky to negotiate and execute a final Offer To Purchase after consultation with counsel. The Board is being asked to approve a transaction whose terms are to be filled in afterward.

The testing equipment item arose because price quotes for portable tables and chairs for mandatory annual testing at Athens and Troy High came in above the Michigan Department of Education's competitive bid threshold, forcing a formal bid. Nine bidders were invited and twelve responded; Global Equipment Co., Inc. was the lowest qualified bidder on BID 9831.

**Other**
Committee assignments adopted in October are revisited because of the Edmunds and Underwood retirements and the two newly elected members. The attached list shows the substitutions made in place — Underwood struck for Hammond on the Diversity Council, Edmunds for Gottlieb on Policy, Fleming for Gottlieb on Superintendent Evaluation, Philippart for Gottlieb on the Oakland Schools Legislative Committee — revised January 17, 2017.

Agenda packet for the organizational and regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, January 17, 2017, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Election of Acting Chairperson; 3. Appointment of Temporary Secretary; 4. Annual Organizational Meeting of the Board of Education — A. Nomination and Election of Officers (President, Vice President, Secretary), B. Appointment of Treasurer, C. Establish Fund Depositories and Investment Resolution, D. Designation of Board and District Legal Counsel, E. Designation of Superintendent to be Deputy Secretary, F. Designation of a Person for Posting Notices of Meetings, G. Meeting Schedule for 2017 Calendar Year; 5. Recognition — A. Board Recognition Month; 6. Additions & Deletions; 7. Public Communication (agenda items); 8. General – Consent Agenda; 9. Personnel — A. Consideration: Employment Dispute Resolution (EDR) Plan; 10. Curriculum; 11. Business — A. Consideration: Section 23 Purchase Agreement, B. Consideration: Portable Testing Tables and Chairs; 12. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 13. Other — A. Consideration: Board Committee Assignments for 2017; 14. Adjournment. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

The agenda index carries the depositories item as covering 2015/16 and 2016/17 — the prior year's range in a January 2017 packet, the same kind of unrevised template text that recurs in these organizational packets.

**The agenda memo.** Richard M. Machesky, Ed.D. writes to the Board. The first order of business is to elect an acting chairperson who will conduct the meeting until a president has been elected, and past practice has been that the previous year's president conducts this part of the meeting. The second order is for the acting chairperson to appoint Judy Holmes to act as temporary secretary until the secretary to the Board has been elected. The acting chairperson then declares nominations in order for president, with the memo noting that nominations need not be seconded, that a motion and support are made to close the nomination, and — set out plainly — that four votes are required for election. The newly elected president declares nominations in order for vice president following the same procedures, then for secretary. On the treasurer, the memo records that according to Board Policy the treasurer is appointed annually by the Board as a nonvoting officer, that the assistant superintendent of business services has served as treasurer, and that the superintendent recommends the procedure continue.

**Organizational items.** Item 2 resolves that a named member serve as acting chairperson to officiate the meeting until the election of a president has been completed. Item 3 suggests the acting chairperson appoint Judy Holmes as temporary secretary. Item 4.A.1 provides the nomination form for president — one member nominating another to serve until December 31, 2017 — followed by the close of nominations and the election resolution, with a roll call listing Schmidt, Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Miletti and Philippart. The same structure repeats for vice president and secretary, with the roll call order rotating so that a different member is called first each time.

The roll call itself is the packet's quiet record of what has changed. Gottlieb and Hammond appear where Edmunds and Underwood stood a month earlier; this is the first meeting of the reconstituted Board.

Item 4.C establishes fund depositories and the investment resolution. The resolution directs Treasurer Rick West to deposit and/or invest all public monies, including tax monies, in his name as Treasurer into Bank of America, Bank of New York, Charter One Bank, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, First Merit Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF (the Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank), Morgan Stanley Smith Barney, PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, and PNC Bank. Monies may be withdrawn by checks signed with the facsimile signature of Treasurer Rick West, and in emergencies the handwritten signature of the Treasurer or of Superintendent Richard M. Machesky, who may sign on the General Fund and Payroll accounts at Bank of America. Accounts at PNC Bank for Troy Career Center expenses are drawn on the handwritten signature of the Career Center Manager, Assistant Manager or Program Coordinators. The Comerica account for health care and dependent care flexible spending claims may be drawn by ACH debit to Next Generation Enrollment, Inc., or by checks bearing the Treasurer's facsimile signature. The Treasurer may open or close accounts with the listed institutions provided it is in the district's interest; funds are invested according to Board Policy 5000.06; the Treasurer is authorized to combine money from more than one fund for an investment authorized by subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code; and the maximum amount to be invested is regulated by the school code. The certification is dated the 17th day of January 2017, with the secretary's name left blank pending that evening's election.

Item 4.D continues the designation of Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Lusk Albertson; LaPointe & Associates, P.C.; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; and Beier Howlett, P.C. as legal counsel to advise and/or represent the Troy School District and Board of Education as necessary for the 2017 calendar year, with the superintendent authorized to consult additional counsel as needed on prior notification to the board. Items 4.E and 4.F designate the superintendent as deputy secretary and a person for posting notices. Item 4.G adopts the meeting schedule for the 2017 calendar year.

The schedule attachment is worth describing as it appears, because it is not a clean document. It is the 2016 calendar overtyped with 2017 dates, both visible in every line: "Tuesday, January 1917, 2016 2017 (Organizational & Regular Meeting)"; "Tuesday, February 1628, 20162017"; "Tuesday, March 1521, 20162017"; "Tuesday, April 1918, 20167"; "Tuesday, May 1716, 20162017"; "Tuesday, June 76, 2016 2017 (location: Athens)"; "Tuesday, June 2120, 20162017"; "Tuesday, July 1918, 20162017"; "Tuesday, August 1615, 20162017"; "Tuesday, September 2019, 20162017"; "Tuesday, October 1817, 20162017"; "Tuesday, November 1521, 20162017"; "Tuesday, December 20, 20162017"; and "Tuesday, January 1716, 2017 2018 (Organizational & Regular Meeting)." The workshop schedule follows the same pattern at the Administrative Center at 6:00 p.m., including a March 2017 workshop at GROW and a Thursday, March 23 winter retreat. A note advises that board meetings are held at the Services Building unless otherwise indicated on the posted agenda and that meeting location should be confirmed in advance via the district website.

**Recognition 5.A: Board of Education Recognition.** Each January the district recognizes and celebrates the work of the Board of Education. The script credits Board members with dedicating an incredible amount of time and energy toward ensuring the best possible educational opportunities for all students, calls them tireless, professional and passionate, and says the community owes them a debt of gratitude.

The gift is tied to a specific idea. One of the first initiatives developed when Machesky was selected to lead the district was the idea of ONE TROY — "that we are not merely a district of schools, but ONE school district, with a single mission and a single focus on student achievement for ALL." Each Board member receives a ONE Troy ensemble, a basket filled with a token of appreciation and pride in each of the district's schools: t-shirts and hats, water bottles and mugs, pens and pencils, and baked goods, each serving as a symbol of one of the schools. The closing line — "From our more senior members to our newest trustees, we are grateful to have each and every one of you" — acknowledges the two new members without naming them.

**Consent minutes: the December 6, 2016 workshop and special meeting.** The workshop, presided over by President Philippart, included the superintendent's update and an Early Childhood Timeline item, adjourning at 9:11 p.m. Board members present were Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood, with administrators Machesky, Birmingham, Dziatczak, Harris and Griffor. The special meeting convened immediately after at 9:12 p.m. with the same members plus administrators Gottlieb, Trotter, Carson and West and approximately 25 members of the audience; its business was a first reading of Board Policy Manual revisions, and it adjourned at 9:18 p.m. The Early Childhood Timeline discussion is the earliest appearance in these packets of the project that would become the Troy School District Preschool.

**Consent minutes: the December 20, 2016 regular meeting.** President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Dr. Philippart, Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Schmidt and Underwood were present; Mr. Miletti was absent, and Superintendent Machesky was also absent. All four high school student representatives attended, along with Deputy Superintendent Mark Dziatczak, administrators Birmingham, Griffor, Harris, Carson, Gottlieb and West, and approximately 50 additional members of the audience.

The evening's recognition honored two of the Board's own, Wendy Underwood and Ida Edmunds, retiring from the Troy Board of Education, this being their final meeting. Dr. Philippart said it is hard to describe the impact these two trustees have had on the community but that it has been tremendous: Wendy leaving after selflessly giving more than 11 years of service to students, staff and families, and Ida retiring after dedicating more than 31 years of her time, talents and passion into learning for all. The minutes note that aside from being an elected position, serving on the Board of Education is also a volunteer position requiring a great deal of time, effort and commitment, and that these two exemplary trustees have done a remarkable service to past and future generations of Troy students. Dr. Philippart presented each with a framed letter from Senator Gary Peters' office and a gift from the Troy School District and School Board. Oakland County Commissioner Wade Fleming was invited up to share kind words and presented each with a proclamation signed by members of the Oakland County Board of Commissioners.

The consent agenda that evening approved the November 1, 2016 workshop minutes, the November 15, 2016 meeting minutes and the October 2016 Treasurer's Reports, 6-0 with Miletti absent. A budget amendment restated the total revenues and unappropriated fund balance estimated to be available for appropriations in the General Fund for fiscal year 2016-17.

Resolution 16-092 awarded bond construction Bid Pack #18, with $2,992,853.00 approved as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund and $369,527.00 as an expenditure of the Food Service Budget. The awards were Blue Star Demolition $14,100.00; Hewett Company exterior doors $537,505.00; Paint Plus painting and floors $35,217.00; Stafford Smith food service equipment $100,063.00; CSM mechanical for Barnard, Bemis, Wass and IAE $873,173.00; Contrast mechanical for Admin, Boulan and Larson $418,000.00; MCMI temperature controls $392,150.00; Great Lakes Power electrical $686,500.00; and contingency $305,672.00 — a total of $3,362,380.00. It carried 6-0.

Resolution 16-093 awarded the roof replacement and restoration bid as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund and the Operational Fund: J. D. Chandler $300,300.00, Royal West $873,316.00 and a 10% contingency of $117,362.00, totalling $1,290,978.00, carried 6-0. Resolution 16-094 approved the adoption of the Troy School District Board of Education Bylaws and Policies, carried 6-0 — the second reading of the revisions first read at the December 6 special meeting.

In public communication on non-agenda items, Mary Bogush, a Royal Oak community member, addressed the Board about the Section 1 property located in Troy that is owned by the Troy School District. She is the same speaker who appears in the March 2018 minutes on the same subject; the Section 1 question was live in this Board's business for at least two years before it was resolved.

Student representative reports included Aman from International Academy-East on mid-term exams and a Personal Project Exhibition for the MYP Middle Years Programme on January 13 from 9 to 11:00 a.m.

**Treasurer's Report, November 2016.** Rick West transmits the check register including current period voids, together with listings of ACH debits, wire transfers and P-Card purchases, certifying that the disbursements were payments made for obligations of the Troy School District and that all materials or services listed on the invoices have been received or performed. By fund: General Fund (101) $4,954,666.13; Grant Fund (120) $21,094.54; Special Education Fund (122) $523,172.32; Durant Funds (140) $239.60; Food Service Fund (520) $368,521.03; Troy Career Center (529) $13,642.30; Community Education Fund (530) $130,491.30; Facilities Rental Fund (535) nil; Debt Funds (306, 312, 314, 315) $1,902.40; Building & Site Funds (499, 414) $607,242.70; Student Activity Fund (700, 701) $193,943.33; Memorial Scholarship Fund (750) nil.

The totals are Total General Fund $5,499,172.59, Total Special Revenue Funds $512,654.63, Total Other Funds $803,088.43, and TOTAL CHECK DISBURSEMENTS $6,814,915.65, plus ACH debits $20,707.64, outgoing wire transfers $1,962,408.22 and P-Card purchases $169,245.62, less prior period void disbursements of $70.00, for TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS IN PERIOD $8,967,207.13. The fund list here differs from later years in two ways worth noting: the Building & Site Funds line names only two funds, 499 and 414, where by 2018 it would name four, and there is no Early Childhood Center fund at all — the project was still a timeline item at a December workshop.

**Personnel 9.A: the Employment Dispute Resolution Plan.** The stated purpose of the EDR Plan is to provide for the fair, efficient and timely resolution of all claims, disputes or controversies arising out of or relating to an application or candidacy for employment, employment and/or cessation of employment, and to provide an applicant or employee with a forum in which claims or disputes with the district may be resolved exclusively by final and binding arbitration rather than litigation.

The resolution recites that the Board has determined it is in the best interest of the district to establish such a plan applicable to all applicants for employment, all substitute employees, all nonunion employees and all nonunion administrators and supervisors employed by the district, and that the Revised School Code, MCL 380.11a, permits a school district to establish an Employment Dispute Resolution Plan. It authorizes the establishment of the plan on that scope, authorizes the Superintendent or his designee to execute the plan documents and any necessary related documents for the Board, and rescinds all conflicting resolutions.

The plan document itself follows. Section 1 restates the purpose and adds an important limit: the EDR Plan does not restrict an applicant or employee from filing a claim or charge with any state, federal or other governmental administrative agency; rather, it applies only to local, state or federal court proceedings. Section 2 provides that all applicants or candidates for employment and all employees not represented by a bargaining unit are subject to the plan, with "employee" defined to include applicants and candidates. Section 3 provides that any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to a covered employee's employment, or a candidate's or applicant's application for employment, or employment contract, shall be settled by arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association, governed by Michigan's Uniform Arbitration Act, MCL 691.1681 et seq., and the AAA Employment Arbitration Rules and Mediation Procedures, with judgment upon the award entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. A collective actions waiver requires employees to individually arbitrate employment disputes. The plan sets a filing window running from a stated event or thirty calendar days from the date the dispute arises.

The scope is precisely drawn around the district's union contracts: everyone the collective bargaining agreements do not already cover — applicants, substitutes, nonunion staff, and the administrators and supervisors who negotiate on the district's behalf — is moved out of court and into AAA arbitration, individually.

**Business 11.A: Section 23 purchase agreement.** The School District issued a Request For Proposals For Purchase of Real Property to obtain proposals to purchase certain surplus vacant real property located in Section 23 adjacent to Raintree Park, and received seven proposals, examined in conjunction with legal counsel Clark Hill and consultant Great Northern. The item recommends that the Board authorize the sale of the property "to the approved developer in the amount of $x,xxx,xxx."

The resolution describes the property as 18.08 +/- acres of vacant land, Sidwell Numbers 20-23-200-007, 20-23-200-008 and 20-23-200-009. It recites that the district has received a proposal from "approved developer (the 'Purchaser')" to purchase the property for a purchase price of "proposed amount ($x,xxx,xxx) Dollars with an earnest money deposit of proposed amount ($xx,xxx) Dollars." It then resolves that the district authorizes the sale on the terms generally described above and substantially similar to those contained in the Purchaser's response and clarifications to the RFP, and authorizes Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky, or his designee, to negotiate the terms and conditions of a final Offer To Purchase with the Purchaser on terms acceptable to the Superintendent after consultation with legal counsel, and to execute the negotiated Offer To Purchase and any and all documents necessary and incidental to the sale.

The placeholders are the substance of the item. Buyer, price and deposit are all left as template text in the published packet, and the operative grant is not approval of a specific transaction but authority for the superintendent to negotiate and execute one on terms he finds acceptable after consulting counsel. Set beside the district's later land sales — where the resolutions name the purchaser, state the price in words and figures, and specify the earnest money — this is a markedly looser instrument, and it is the first of the surplus-property sales that would run through 2018.

**Business 11.B: portable testing tables and chairs.** An RFP was issued for competitive bids on portable testing tables and chairs, reviewed by Todd Hensley, Purchasing Supervisor. Hensley's memorandum to Rick West explains the origin: upon receiving several price quotes during research on portable tables and chairs for mandatory annual testing at both Athens and Troy High Schools, it became apparent that the cost of this testing equipment was above the Michigan Department of Education's competitive bid threshold, so a formal bid was processed. Invitations were sent to nine potential bidders to provide closed sealed pricing; twelve responses were received. After analyzing the proposals, the lowest qualified bidder was Global Equipment Co., Inc. He recommends awarding BID 9831 – Portable Tables and Chairs – Testing Equipment to Global Equipment Co., Inc. in the amount of $101,162.00 as detailed in the attached bid tabulation. The resolution awards the bid to Global Equipment Co., Inc. in the amount of $101,162.00 as an expenditure of the general fund.

More bids came back than invitations went out — twelve responses to nine invitations — which the memo notes without comment.

**Other 13.A: 2017 Board committee assignments.** Board Committee Assignments for the 2016-17 school year were adopted at the October 18 Board Meeting; however, due to the retirement of Ida Edmunds and Wendy Underwood and the two newly elected Board members joining, the Board needed to revisit the assignments, which were discussed and agreed upon at the January 10 workshop. The resolution adopts the Board Committee Memberships for the remainder of the 2016-2017 school year as attached.

The attached list is a revision of the October document with the departing members' names struck through and the new ones substituted in place, so both appear: the Diversity Council reads "UnderwoodHammon[d]"; the Policy Committee reads "EdmundsGottlieb" alongside Hauff and Philippart; the Superintendent Evaluation Committee reads "FlemingGottlieb" alongside Schmidt and Miletti; and the Oakland Schools' Legislative Committee and Designate read "PhilippartGottlieb/Hauff." The Crisis Committee stays with Miletti. The document is footed "Revised: January 17, 2017."

Read as a whole, the January 2017 packet is a Board reconstituting itself. Two trustees with more than forty years of combined service left in December; two new ones are seated here, and the committee sheet, the roll call and the recognition script all register the change. Around that, the meeting does three pieces of durable business: it routes every nonunion employment dispute out of the courts and into individual arbitration, it buys the furniture that state-mandated testing requires, and it opens the sale of eighteen acres on a resolution that names neither the buyer nor the price.
